record.tranche_reason: The post reports SAE sparsity and reconstruction measurements, but does not directly measure polysemanticity or test any listed version.
record.gate_note: The reported measurements are SAE reconstruction MSE, mean L1, and percentage of features active. They describe sparsity, not whether neurons respond to unrelated inputs; the author's interpretation about needing less polysemanticity is speculative.
record.test_reason: The post compares two ~3.7M transformers (normal vs input-computed MLP bias) using SAE reconstruction MSE, mean L1 and fraction of SAE features active. None of these measures whether individual neurons respond to unrelated inputs, so no version is tested. The link to polysemanticity is the author's speculation.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct: the author found Flexbias sparser and speculates it needs less polysemanticity, but calls this take unsatisfying and wants more experiments.
record.recipe_differences: The post compares normal and input-computed bias using SAE sparsity-related measurements; it does not reproduce the original method.

fits_no_version.finding: Flexbias model gave lower SAE mean L1 (0.127 vs 0.294) and fewer SAE features active (38.3% vs 49.5%), but higher reconstruction MSE (0.0116 vs 0.0051).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Making the MLP bias input-dependent in a small transformer is associated with sparser SAE codes but worse SAE reconstruction.

record.problems: The post gives no uncertainty estimates or controls, and does not directly measure polysemanticity or task performance. It reports one comparison and describes the proposed explanation as unsatisfactory.

untested.parts: Architecture change (Flexbias) is made, but no share of polysemantic neurons and no task performance are measured.
No neuron-level responses to unrelated tokens or contexts are measured.
Superposition and capacity pressure are not tested.

record.verdict_notes: Single comparison, no uncertainty, no controls. Lower mean L1 alongside higher MSE may simply reflect a different reconstruction–sparsity trade-off, not reduced polysemanticity. The layer studied and the SAE training details are not stated.

versions.untested_parts: No vision model or neuron response to image inputs is examined.
No language-model neurons are tested for responses to unrelated tokens or contexts.
The post does not test superposition or capacity pressure.
The post does not test initialization, regularization, training noise, or neuron-level polysemanticity.
Flexbias changes how bias is obtained, but the post does not measure polysemantic neurons or report model task performance.
No neuron features or shared jobs are examined.
No alternative activation ranges or explanation-scoring methods are compared.
